Definition: from G3361 and G5037; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even:--neither, (n-)or, so as much.
BiblicalUsage: Paul piles up the neither-nors: teachers of the law who understand neither what they say nor what they affirm, and a day of Christ that is not at hand, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter. The word chains denials together, and Paul uses it to fence off error from every side at once.
TheologicalSignificance: I take Paul's doubled negatives as a model for discernment: error rarely comes from one direction, so the truth has to be guarded on every side, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter.
